## Summary

Discovered by the Step 7 parity sweep while fixing `fernlike-toothsome-hen` (79b2-6ebc-6c1d-4125),
where the MCP edge emitted `307` with a plaintext `http://` Location on the documented client URL.

The **rule** that bug established: *an https request to this edge must never receive a `Location`
header that downgrades the scheme to `http`.* That rule is now enforced for the MCP paths only.
The other proxied surfaces on the same port-443 server have no equivalent guarantee.

## Channel census (`infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template`)

| surface | Location-scheme guarantee |
|---|---|
| `location = /mcp/`, `= /mcp`, prefix `/mcp` | ENFORCED by 79b2 (`proxy_redirect` http->https) |
| `location /review/` (`:92`) | **MISSING** |
| `location /opcert/` (`:107`) | **MISSING** |
| `location /` -> Gerrit (`:152`) | **MISSING** |
| port-80 server | N/A — correctly `301`s to https |

HSTS is NOT part of this gap: 79b2 adds `add_header Strict-Transport-Security ... always;` at the
443 **server** level, so every surface above already inherits that backstop.

## Why it was left out of 79b2's scope

The obvious fix — hoisting `proxy_redirect` to the server level — is NOT safe as a drop-in.
`proxy_redirect` defaults to `default`, which derives its rewrite from **that location's own**
`proxy_pass`. `/review/` uses `proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:${REVIEW_BOT_PORT}/;` (a
prefix-stripping form), so its `default` rule rewrites the upstream's `http://127.0.0.1:PORT/`
Location back to `/review/`. Declaring explicit server-level rules would REPLACE that default and
could break the review-bot's relative redirects. Gerrit's block additionally carries a standing
"do not add a rewrite here" constraint for `%2F`-safe proxying (`:145-151`) — `proxy_redirect`
only touches response headers, never the request URI, so it is very likely safe there, but that
needs to be established rather than assumed.

So the correct fix is per-surface and needs its own verification, which is more than 79b2's
blast radius should carry.

## Severity

Lower than 79b2. No plaintext Location has been OBSERVED from these three surfaces; this is a
missing structural guarantee, not a reproduced downgrade. The 79b2 root cause B
(`FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS` unset, so uvicorn distrusts the forwarded proto) applies specifically to
the containerised MCP service; `/review/` and `/opcert/` should be checked for the same posture
rather than presumed affected or unaffected.

## Root cause (CONFIRMED — supersedes the "not reproduced" severity note above)

The downgrade IS reproduced, on `/review/`, unauthenticated, against the deployed edge:

    GET https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/review/health/
      -> HTTP/2 307, location: http://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/health

(`/review/webhook/` and `/review/rerun/` behave identically.) Full evidence in the Phase-1-exit
RCA comment.

Mechanism — this is 79b2's **root cause B on two more services**, answering this ticket's own open
question: `FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS` is set only for the `mcp` service (`docker-compose.yml:357`,
`autodeploy.sh:380`) and is **unset** for `review-bot` (`:75`) and `opcert` (`:266`). uvicorn
defaults it to `"127.0.0.1"` and wraps each app in `ProxyHeadersMiddleware(trusted_hosts=<that>)`.
Both run in containers published on host loopback (`:97`, `:298`), so nginx connects from the
docker bridge gateway, the peer is untrusted, `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` is dropped,
`scope["scheme"]` stays `"http"`, and Starlette's `redirect_slashes` builds an absolute
`URL(scope=…)` at `http://`. Flipping only the trust list flips only the scheme, for both apps.

Gerrit is NOT affected by that mechanism: it builds absolute Locations from
`canonicalWebUrl = https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/` (`infra/compose/gerrit.config:14`) and
already emits https (`/settings` -> `https://…/settings/`). Its guarantee is a config value that
nothing at the edge enforces, so it still warrants the backstop.

## Approach

Two layers, mirroring exactly what 79b2 did for MCP:

1. **Root cause** — `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`: set `FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS: "*"` on
   `review-bot` and `opcert`, so each app trusts nginx's forwarded proto and stops building
   `http://` URLs at the source. `"*"` rather than a pinned bridge-gateway address for the same
   reason the `mcp` service documents: neither service declares a `networks:` block, so that
   address is implicit and can drift, and a stale pin re-opens the downgrade with no failure
   signal. Trust-all is bounded here — both ports are published on host **loopback** with nginx
   the sole reachable client, and nginx sets `X-Forwarded-Proto https` as a **literal** that
   overwrites anything a client sends, so the value cannot be forged.
2. **Structural backstop** — `infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template`: add `proxy_redirect` http->https
   rules to `/review/` (`:103`), `/opcert/` (`:118`) and Gerrit's `location /` (`:253`).
   **Per-location, never server-level** — 79b2's binding precedent, because a server-level rule
   would REPLACE each location's `default`. Each block therefore restates `proxy_redirect
   default;` FIRST, since nginx drops the implicit default as soon as any explicit rule appears in
   a location; that is what preserves `/review/`'s prefix-stripping default rewrite.

`proxy_redirect` rewrites only the `Location`/`Refresh` **response** headers. It is not a
`rewrite` and adds no URI path to `proxy_pass`, so it cannot affect Gerrit's `%2F`-safe request
proxying, which is governed by the standing constraint at `rebar.conf.template:245-252`.

Deliberately out of scope: `/review/`'s Location also loses the `/review/` prefix
(`…/review/health/` -> `…/health`). That is path correctness, not a scheme downgrade, and is filed
as a sibling via `discovered_from`.

## Testing

- Happy path: the RENDERED config (template through `envsubst '${REVIEW_BOT_PORT}'`) shows each of
  the three locations carrying both the `$host` and the upstream-form http->https `proxy_redirect`
  rules.
- Edge: each of the three restates `proxy_redirect default;` before its explicit rules, so no
  implicit default is dropped — the direct evidence for `/review/`'s prefix-stripping rewrite
  surviving.
- Compose posture: `review-bot` and `opcert` each set `FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS` to exactly `"*"`,
  asserted against the committed `docker-compose.yml` the way the existing `mcp` test does.
- Mutation check: deleting each new rule / env value in turn must turn the corresponding test RED.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] For each of `/review/`, `/opcert/` and Gerrit's `location /`, it is established and
      recorded whether that upstream can emit an absolute `http://` Location — by inspecting how
      each app builds redirects and whether it sits behind a proxy-headers trust boundary.
- [x] Every surface that CAN emit one carries a `proxy_redirect` rule upgrading it to `https`,
      added per-location so no existing `default` rule is replaced. Verified by a structural test
      over `infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template` that fails if a surface regresses.
- [x] `/review/`'s existing `default` proxy_redirect behaviour is preserved — evidenced by
      showing the prefix-stripping rewrite still applies after the change.
- [x] Gerrit's `%2F`-safe proxying is unaffected, evidenced by reasoning or a probe that
      `proxy_redirect` alters only response headers and not the request URI.
- [x] LIVE VALIDATION [non-codebase]: an unauthenticated probe of each surface on the deployed edge shows no `http://` Location. MET 2026-09-01 via the operator-authorized edge deploy; actual response headers + full provenance recorded in a ticket comment below.

## Notes

Reported from unauthenticated probes and repo inspection only. No credential was transmitted.
